title: Finiteness over a space point passes from an etale covering to affine etale charts
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $x\in|X|$ be a field-valued point class [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Let $(a_i:U_i\to X)_{i\in I}$ be a set-indexed jointly surjective family of representable etale morphisms from schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism]: the union of the images of $|U_i|\to|X|$ is $|X|$. Suppose each set $|a_i|^{-1}(\{x\})$ is finite. Then for every affine scheme $V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and every representable etale morphism $v:V\to X$, the set $|v|^{-1}(\{x\})$ is finite. The schemes $U_i$ need not be affine or quasi-compact, and their fibres at $x$ may be empty. No assumption on the fibres of $U_i\times_XU_i$ is made.

proof.text: Fix an affine etale chart $v:V\to X$. Form the schemes $P_i=V\times_XU_i$, with projections $q_i:P_i\to V$ and $p_i:P_i\to U_i$. Representability makes $p_i$, the base change of $v$, etale. Base change of the given covering makes the $q_i$ etale and jointly surjective. Thus every point of $V$ lifts to some $P_i$.

source.place: Tag 03JS, first fibre-product diagrams; spaces.tex Tags 02X2/04T9 and spaces-topologies.tex Tag 041F(3).

proof.text: Cover each $P_i$ by its affine open subschemes $W$. Each image $q_i(W)$ is open, because $q_i$ is etale and hence an open map. These images cover $V$. Since an affine scheme is quasi-compact, choose finitely many such pairs $(i_j,W_j)$, $1\leq j\leq n$, whose images cover $V$. Each $W_j$ is quasi-compact by the same spectrum compactness theorem. This does not require any $P_i$ or $U_i$ to be quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 03JS, finite quasi-compact open refinement; schemes.tex Tag 01IT; morphisms.tex Tag 03WT; algebra.tex Tag 00E8.

proof.text: For each chosen pair set $r_j=p_{i_j}|_{W_j}:W_j\to U_{i_j}$. Since etale maps are unramified, $p_{i_j}$ is locally quasi-finite; restriction to an open preserves this. Apply the quasi-compact-source bounded-fibre theorem to $r_j$. For every $u\in U_{i_j}$ its scheme fibre is finite over $\kappa(u)$, so has finitely many points: apply finite-morphism finite fibres to its projection to the one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$. The scheme fibre projects homeomorphically onto $r_j^{-1}(u)$. Hence each set $r_j^{-1}(u)$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 03JS, application of Tag 03JA; morphisms.tex Tags 02V5 and 01TH(4); finite fibres Tag 02NH; schemes.tex Tag 01K1.

proof.text: Put $F_i=|a_i|^{-1}(\{x\})$. It is finite by hypothesis, and $B_j=r_j^{-1}(F_{i_j})=\bigcup_{u\in F_{i_j}}r_j^{-1}(u)$ is finite by step 3. Its image in $V$ lies above $x$, since $v q_{i_j}=a_{i_j}p_{i_j}$. Conversely, if $t\in|V|$ maps to $x$, the covering in step 2 gives $j$ and $w\in W_j$ with $q_{i_j}(w)=t$. The same equality puts $r_j(w)$ in $F_{i_j}$, so $w\in B_j$. Therefore $|v|^{-1}(\{x\})=\bigcup_{j=1}^n q_{i_j}(B_j)$ is a finite union of finite images. Empty $F_i$ contribute empty sets; if $V$ is empty the conclusion is immediate.

source.place: Tag 03JS, last sentence: finite unions and images, with the point-surjectivity already supplied in steps 1 and 2.
